meta.purpose: R-72: the clear list of questions, information and answers that must be settled before a decision based on this data is reasonable. Each row states what is already established, what is missing, and the specific information that would close it.
meta.answer_rule: Where the answer is not established by an official source read this session, the answer column is blank and the row carries an unverified marker. No answer is inferred.

rows: Which market price source will we use, and under what licence?
No official NFL page publishes betting prices. nfl.com publishes schedule, scores, standings and injuries only.
The whole price layer: open, close, consensus, vig.
A written licence or terms-of-use decision naming the price vendor and what may be stored and republished.
Can we store raw market prices, or only derived residuals?
The owner's data policy, which R-20 says must be decided before any backtest is published.
A one-line policy: store raw, store derived only, or store neither.
Blocks R-20 and every ROI and CLV number
What is the official closing price, and at what timestamp?
Timestamp convention for 'close' - kickoff, or last pre-kickoff refresh.
The vendor's definition of close, with a timestamp field we capture.
How is vig removed, and whose consensus is the benchmark?
Undecided. R-60 asks for a vig-free decomposition before any bet structure is considered.
The de-vig method and the consensus set.
A named de-vig formula and the list of books in the consensus.
Is there one official depth-chart source covering all 32 clubs?
nfl.com publishes an official injury report; this session found no league-wide depth-chart page on nfl.com.
A verified source for 32 of 32 clubs.
R-52 route (a): a dated per-club depth page for each of the 32 clubs, checked club by club.
Does an official snap-count source exist, and can it be captured?
R-52 route (b). Snap counts are also the R-56 starter proxy.
Confirmation that an official snap-count feed exists and is capturable, or a written decision to close route (b).
How often must the injury report be captured for a surprise feature?
This session captured 1 report on 1 day. The report page offers a season selector back to 1965 and a week selector for the current season.
Wed, Thu and Fri captures with fetch timestamps (R-54, R-55).
A scheduled collector running 3 times weekly, retaining hashes.
What is the play rate for each game designation, with confidence intervals?
This session's capture has 171 designated rows: 90 Questionable, 70 Out, 11 Doubtful. No outcome is joined to them yet.
R-53: designations joined to official inactives over several seasons.
Official inactive lists for at least 3 seasons, joined to the designations.
Where does the official inactive list live, and is it capturable per fixture?
nfl.com publishes weekly inactives articles, for example the Week 9 inactives page linked from the official injury page.
A per-fixture, dated capture of the inactive list.
A parser for the weekly inactives article, run per week.
Who actually started, per fixture, from an official source?
No game book parsed this session. Actual starters confirmed for 0 of 150 fixtures.
R-25: official NFL Game Books for actual starters.
A game-book parser, per R-25 and prior sessions' open request.
How do we version depth against roster turnover?
This session captured 5 dated roster/IR events from official nfl.com news headlines.
A transactions feed to version against (R-34, R-46).
Either an official transactions log feed, or a decision to version from the dated news articles alone.
No. This session captured IR evidence for named players from official news; a full reserve list is not captured (R-64).
A reserve-list or IR feed covering 32 clubs.
A decision on which official page is the authoritative reserve list.
Blocks R-64, and biases any net-injury count
May row-level official data be committed to a public repository?
This namespace commits a structured capture of the official injury report. Prior sessions in this repository disagree on this point.
The owner's reading of the terms.
A written decision, recorded as flag RF-05.
Blocks R-40 and the private/public split
What derived analysis may be published?
Standings, results, schedule facts and injury designations are read from nfl.com and republished here as analysis.
The line between derived analysis and row-level republication.
The same written decision as Q-13.
How many graded games before a strategy can be ranked?
The governance rule says n >= 300 prospective graded games.
Nothing is missing; this is a settled threshold.
Not required - the threshold is published and enforced.
What is the benchmark for Brier skill?
Undecided. The rule says benchmark-relative, and the control baselines C1 and C2 are defined.
Which benchmark: control baseline, market consensus, or a fixed base rate.
A named benchmark, written down before the first graded run.
How is the multiplicity adjustment computed as strategies accumulate?
The rule specifies a multiplicity adjustment for the number of trials.
The exact adjustment rule as the number of registered strategies grows.
A written adjustment formula tied to the count of registered strategies.
Which seasons are train, validation and final holdout?
Only 2026 through Week 10 is ingested. R-70 needs 3 completed seasons.
Historical seasons 2023, 2024 and 2025, ingested at game level.
A bulk backfill of at least 3 completed seasons from the official schedule pages.
Do we run the ablation with or without the personnel features first?
The ablation spec is frozen (R-27, R-28) but requires 4 dated weeks of availability history; 1 exists.
3 more weeks of dated availability captures.
The scheduled collector from Q-07 running for 4 consecutive weeks.
Where do immutable snapshots live, and who is alerted when they go stale?
Hashes are computed and published locally this session; no off-site store and no alerting exist (R-39).
A durable store outside the static site, plus a freshness alert.
An owner decision on the store, then a scheduled job with an alert channel.
What happens when a scraper's row count drifts?
Implemented: verify.py pins expected row counts and required fields and fails the build when a field goes missing (R-63).
Nothing is missing for this namespace.
Not required - the alarm exists and runs.
How do we get the venue of every fixture from the official game centre?
150 fixtures are ingested with a game-centre link each. 0 venues have been transcribed (R-23).
A game-centre parser run per fixture.
A parser for the game-centre page, run over all 150 fixtures.
Which venues are neutral or international sites?
The official schedule labels international games and names the host city for 5 fixtures across Weeks 1-10 and 1 in Week 11.
The stadium for each neutral site, from the game centre.
Blocks R-23 and the weather overlay
What is the official roof designation and surface per stadium, and how far ahead is it published?
Not read this session. The brief cites a 90-minute pre-kickoff roof designation (R-58).
The official stadium page and the roof-status feed.
A source for roof status per fixture, plus a surface field per stadium.
How is the NWS hourly grid joined to each fixture?
The grid-to-venue join and the forecast horizon.
A documented join from venue coordinates to the NWS grid, validated on one week.
What changed in the 2026 kickoff and onside-kick rules, in the league's own words?
Not located and read this session (flag RF-06). R-68 asks for a regime-priors filter.
The official rule-change document, fetched and quoted, before the filter is built.
Where is the league's dated schedule announcement published?
The live official schedule is published by week. The dated announcement article is not fetched this session (flag RF-07).
R-24: the dated announcement beside the live schedule.
The announcement article URL, fetched and dated.
What is the demotion threshold that sends a live strategy back to paper?
The governance page publishes the threshold; no strategy is live, so it has never fired (R-08).
Not required until a strategy goes live.
Blocks R-08 only once a strategy is live
How are rewards funded and paid?
Reward tiers are published; 0 strategies are reward-eligible (R-74).
The funding decision and the payout rule tied to the prospective escrow.
A written reward schedule from the owner.
Which workspace in this repository is canonical?
This repository contains roughly 50 prior NFL workspaces that overlap heavily. This session added one more rather than editing any of them.
An owner decision naming one canonical workspace.
A written choice, recorded so future sessions stop adding namespaces.
Blocks nothing, but multiplies review cost
